transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Well… I guess what brings me in is my eating, doctor. It’s not just that I like food or that I get hungry. It’s more like, once I start eating certain comfort foods, I can’t seem to stop myself the way I used to think a person should be able to.

Like I’ll be there at the stove or by the pot, and I’ll tell myself, “Maria, that is enough now. Put it away.” I really do say that to myself. But then my hand just goes back again, like it’s moving before I’ve fully decided. And I feel embarrassed saying that at my age, but it feels like I’m not in charge in those moments. I know I’ve had enough, but I keep taking more. That’s the part that scares me a little, I suppose… that feeling that I can’t make myself stop once I’ve started.

Maria, can you tell me a bit more about those times when you feel like you can’t stop eating—do you usually end up eating a lot more than you planned, and do you ever try to make up for it afterward, like skipping meals or exercising a lot?

Yes… yes, I do end up eating a lot more than I meant to. It’s usually not like I sit down thinking I’m going to do that. It starts normal, you know? Like some afternoons after choir, or if I’ve been out in the garden pulling weeds and I come in tired, I’ll fix myself a plate—rice and beans, maybe some chicken stew if I made a pot—and I tell myself it’s just lunch or an early supper.

But then I finish the plate and I go back, just a little more at first. Then maybe I stand there by the stove and take another scoop, and another. Before I really face what I’m doing, I’ve eaten enough like it could have been two meals, sometimes even three. And I feel so foolish afterward because I know nobody needs that much, but in the moment I keep thinking, “Well, just this bit more,” and then it isn’t just a bit anymore.
Maria, after these times when you feel like you've eaten much more than you intended, do you ever make yourself sick or use laxatives to get rid of the food?

I… I don’t really know how to answer that exactly. I mean, I’ve felt terribly full and ashamed afterward, and sometimes I’ll sit there thinking, “Why did I do that to myself?” But making myself sick on purpose… I’m not sure that’s something I can say I do.

And laxatives—no, I don’t have anything particular to tell you there. I know people talk about those things, but for me it’s more that I just feel awful afterward and then I try to get through the rest of the day. I don’t have some plan after, if that makes sense. I mostly just feel upset with myself.

Maria, do these episodes of eating more than you intend tend to interfere with your daily life—like making you avoid social situations, feel depressed, or keep you from doing things you normally enjoy?

Yes… in a way it does, though I try not to let it take over my whole life. I still go to Mass, and I still go to choir, and I keep up with my house as best I can. I don’t want you to think I’m just sitting alone all the time or that I’ve stopped doing everything, because I haven’t.

But after one of those afternoons, when I’ve eaten like that and I’m feeling full and ashamed, I do tend to close myself off. I’ll think about calling someone from church, or maybe returning a call, and then I just… don’t. I’ll tell myself I’m tired, or I’ll do it tomorrow, but really it’s because I feel embarrassed, even if nobody saw me. I feel like it shows on me somehow, or like I don’t want to have to sound cheerful when I feel so disappointed in myself.

So yes, I still do the main things I’m supposed to do, but on those days I’m more likely to stay in, keep quiet, not reach out to people. It makes my world a little smaller for that day, I suppose.

Maria, when you find yourself eating more than you intended, does it feel like you’ve lost control over your eating during those episodes—like you’re unable to stop or regulate what or how much you’re eating?

Yes… that’s really the part that scares me, I think. It does feel like I lose control. I’ll be standing there with those comfort foods—things I know I like too much, the stews, the rice, whatever is warm and filling—and I’ll tell myself, Maria, that’s enough now. You’ve had your plate, put the spoon down.

And I mean it when I say it to myself. It’s not like I don’t know. I do know. But then my hand just goes back to the pot anyway, like before I’ve even fully decided. I’ll take another spoonful, and then another little bit, and I keep trying to make it sound small in my head—just a taste, just finish that piece, just even it out—but it keeps going.

So yes, it feels like I can’t regulate it in that moment. I can talk to myself very sternly, like I would talk to one of my children when they were young, but it doesn’t stop my hand from going back. That’s what brings me in, really. Not just that I eat, but that once I start, I can’t seem to make myself stop when I know I should.

Maria, have these episodes ever caused you significant distress or affected your ability to function in your daily responsibilities, such as caring for your home, being with family, or participating in activities at church?

Yes… it does distress me, definitely. I wouldn’t say I stop everything, because I don’t. I still go to Mass, and I still go to choir, and I do try to keep my home in order. Those things matter to me, and I suppose I’m stubborn enough that I don’t want this to take them away from me.

But after one of those afternoons, when I’ve eaten too much and I’m sitting there feeling embarrassed and disappointed in myself, I tend to pull back. I might have meant to call someone, or answer the phone, or maybe go do a small errand, and instead I just stay in. I tell myself, “Oh, I’ll do it later,” but really I don’t want to be around anyone. I feel ashamed, even if nobody knows what happened.

So it doesn’t make me unable to take care of everything, no… but it does affect me. It makes me quieter, more closed off, and I don’t reach out the way I normally would.
Maria, do you ever find yourself eating these larger amounts of food in secret because you're embarrassed about how much you're eating?

I’m not sure I would call it secret exactly… I mean, I live my own life, so a lot of my eating is just me by myself anyway. There isn’t always someone there to hide it from, if that makes sense.

But embarrassed, yes, I do feel embarrassed. If someone were to walk in and see the amount, I would feel awful. I think I’d probably try to make it look like less than it was, or put things away quickly. Not because I’m trying to be dishonest, but because it feels very private and shameful in that moment.

So… I don’t know if I plan it like, “I’m going to sneak food now.” It’s more that when it happens, I’m relieved no one is there seeing it. And afterward I don’t exactly want to tell anyone about it.
